blindSummary: A 2026 law (enacted 18 Feb 2026 over the governor's veto) confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in government buildings and creates a private right of action allowing anyone to sue a person they suspect of violating it for ~$1,000 in damages — a bounty-hunter mechanism that exposes visitors directly; the law also invalidates state-issued IDs with corrected markers (existing licences void from 26 Feb 2026, no grace period, holders notified in writing) and bars future updates. This state/province was the first raised to the top 'avoid entirely' grade of the international legal-risk map this cycle; two trans men sued within days citing fear of violence.
blindSourceSummaries: A civil-liberties union guide (27 Feb 2026) on the 2026 law: prohibits trans people from updating gender markers on state-issued driver's licences/state IDs and invalidates existing state-issued documents reflecting a gender different from sex at birth — void as of 26 Feb 2026 with no grace period, with the licensing department required to notify affected holders; explains facility-use restrictions, penalties and the out-of-state-ID position.

July 2026 edition of the anti-trans national legal-risk assessment map: this state/province remains in the top 'avoid entirely' grade (with three other states, one newly added in this edition); documents its bathroom-restriction-plus-private-suit design as among the most severe instruments affecting cross-state travel.

February 2026 edition: this state/province became the cycle's first addition to the top 'avoid entirely' grade after enacting a bounty-style law that allows private individuals to sue transgender people encountered in restrooms for substantial sums of money, which could meaningfully affect travel across state lines; the same edition elevated two other states, and — for international visitors — designated the whole country 'avoid entirely' absent an understanding of the legal environment, citing visa-revocation and detention risk.
